Everything on the north wall must be authored at depth >= NF = 0.36. A consequence used deliberately this round: because you never see this room's own north wall from inside it, an opening cut here shows the ARCADE's wall face unless the Arcade cuts one too -- so the relocated door carries a closed six-panel leaf at local z 0.36-0.50, which is what the photographs show anyway and which hides the unpaired hole until room 2 is cut.

_wall_tone_disagreement: I did not do half of prescription 2, and here is why. Deleting the per-wall skins and painting one albedo does not give a 21-byte corner break, it gives 78: measured this round, one grey renders N 240.1 / W 218.9 / E 173.7 / S 180.5 at albedo 255 and N 190.3 / W 147.1 / E 66.3 / S 112.1 at albedo 122. The photograph's break is 13.5 ('v3 4' west 182.9 vs south 169.4) and 20.9 ('Movie room' north 205.6 vs west 184.7). So four skins stay -- but they are no longer four paints solved to force one number: they are one TARGET LADDER (N 190 / W 183 / E 172 / S 168) inverted through each wall's own measured response, which is what any tone-matched render has to do in a scene with one sun and no bounce. Achieved N 189.1 / W 190.7 / E 175.9 / S 166.3, spread 24.4, mean 180.5, against the primary photograph's 169.4-182.9. SECOND disagreement: the critic gives the photograph's chair-rail step as 9%. Metered on a clean box in 'v3 4' -- west upper 182.9 vs west wainscot 153.5 -- it is 16.1%; in 'Movie room' west it is 13.1%. The rail's PHYSICAL relief was halved anyway, since that is a real defect, but the built value step of 11.8-18.9% is deliberately not 9%. THIRD: the critic's exposure table quotes photo wall upper 205 while its own gradient table quotes 148.5/169.5 from 'v3 4' -- those are two different exposures of the same room (their ceilings meter 189.6 and 161.0, 29 bytes apart). The build targets between them, leaning bright.

_camera.why: cutaway.js fades the two walls nearest the camera. This room's content is on the NORTH wall (TV, console, subs, door) and the WEST wall (print, both windows, sectional) -- doll_se culls SOUTH and EAST and is the only quadrant that leaves both standing. The stair partition is >1 ft from any room wall so cutaway leaves it alone, which is right: it is a real interior wall.

_how_the_wall_skins_were_solved: Two-point probe with the SHIPPED emissive in place: build the four skins at grey 255, shoot look_n/s/e/w, meter the four clean boxes; rebuild at grey 122, shoot, meter. Inside [122, 255] the render byte is close enough to linear in the albedo byte to invert directly. Measured: N (240.1, 190.3), W (218.9, 147.1), E (173.7, 66.3), S (180.5, 112.1). The NORTH wall is strongly NON-linear below that -- a near-black skin metered 77.7 where a two-point linear fit predicts ~174 -- so its wainscot inverts through a third measured point at albedo 36. The ramp is expressed as an albedo-BYTE drop from chair rail to crown (N 45, W 70, E 30, S 62 on the upper band; N 24, W 36, E 16, S 32 on the wainscot); the material carries the bottom albedo and Part.colors walks it down, which works because glb.py runs COLOR_0 through srgb->linear on export, so a colour c multiplies the albedo BYTE by c. The SOUTH wall renders 161.3 at pure white with no emissive and cannot be painted brighter, so all four skins carry a small uniform non-coloured emissive #4e4e4e -- full-wall and corner-to-corner, so it reads as paint value and not as the hard-edged partial 'wall wash' ROOM-BRIEF bans. Exception: the EAST skin carries none, because its response was probed on the stair partition (the east-facing surface you actually see) and the two must agree or the join between them shows a seam.
_contact_shadows: `cshadow()` takes the piece's HALF-EXTENTS and runs a ramp from 0.55x them out to (h + out) with exponent 1.15, in 16 OVERLAPPING coplanar discs each at alpha 1-(1-strength)^(1/16). CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: round 2's entry here described this as 'one coplanar layer of non-overlapping annuli'. That was wrong about its own code -- the layers overlap, and that is the mechanism: the darkening at radius r is 1-(1-a)^(layers covering r). Measured in the top-down plan render against clean rug at 206: 30% darkening at the ottoman's contact edge easing to zero over ~16 px, 43-48% under the swivel chairs. Round 2 shipped 10 layers, which put ~5 blend steps across a 0.8 ft ramp and made the rings countable at eye level; 16 puts a step every ~0.05 ft. Heights: floor plane 0.042, rug 0.046-0.098, shadows on bare plank 0.058, shadows on the rug 0.104 -- all clear of the slab's polygonOffset.
_gaps: *** THE DOOR IS UNPAIRED. *** Room 1's opening 3 is now edge 0 / offset 17.30 / width 3.10 = world x 15.40-18.50. The Arcade's opening 103 is still at world x 11.40-14.10. Neither hole shows the other room until room 2 is re-cut to edge_index 2, offset 0.10, width 3.10. I was told not to touch room 2. The closed six-panel leaf built at local z 0.36-0.50 hides this from inside the Movie Room, and the photographs show that door closed, so nothing looks broken from here -- but from the Arcade side there is a hole into this room's wall face at the old position and a blind wall at the new one.

The EAST wall's upper band has the weakest vertical ramp (slope 4.3 per 100 px against the photographs' 14-35). It is at the albedo ceiling: 253 of 255 is already needed just to hit the target mean, so the ramp can only run downward from white and a bigger one would cost ~20 bytes of mean. Fixing this properly needs either more emissive headroom or a brighter scene.

The CEILING meters det_sd 5.0 -- but that box straddles a recessed can's falloff; the flat field is closer to 1. A downward plane at 8 ft minifies its tile almost to flat colour. Left alone rather than cranking tile contrast, which would show as a visible mosaic from the doll pose.
The five-panel print is a procedurally generated dark-massed-figures image, not the owner's actual artwork, and at close range it reads as blobs rather than a battle scene.

The 2nd flat TV was moved from the stair partition to the EAST wall at local z 17.60-21.30 (v3 5 and v3 3 both put it on the wall south of the stair foot). Its exact z is a camera estimate, +/- 1.5 ft.

The south-east prop cluster (black cabinet, ring fan, wire rack, side table) was re-solved from the v3 4 south-wall camera map to local x 12.1-16.9. That map is fitted, not surveyed; the ORDER (fan east of cabinet, rack and table west of it) is certain from the photograph, the absolute x is good to maybe +/- 1.5 ft.
Not modelled: the white electrical panel, the thermostat, the smoke detector, the return register and the console's exact hardware.
